claims.text: The starting solution contains uniformly dispersed noble-metal ions such as Pt, Pd, Au, Ag, and Ru prior to reduction.
Controlled low-temperature reduction and dropwise mixing suppress free precursor mobility.
Restricted precursor mobility promotes homogeneous mixing of five or more noble metals.
Five-element mixtures form a single phase more readily than binary alloys under relevant low-mobility formation conditions.
Reduction kinetics and precursor steady-state times govern whether quinary noble-metal nanocrystals become homogeneous alloys or compositionally structured particles.
The proposed synthesis produces a narrow compositional distribution with minimized phase segregation.
Homogeneous atomic mixing produces highly dispersed, isolated noble-metal active sites.
Isolated noble-metal sites interact synergistically and thereby improve catalytic performance.
Lower synthesis temperature inhibits precursor mobility.
Limited free-atom mobility increases the probability that multiple element types are incorporated stochastically into a random single-phase alloy.
High mixing entropy stabilizes the homogeneous nanoparticle structure.
Charge transfer and local electronic synergy among the constituent metals and minor alloying species enhance catalytic reactivity.
The five-metal HEA will have significantly higher turnover frequency and selectivity than a binary alloy synthesized by the same protocol.
The five-metal HEA will have higher compositional uniformity than a binary alloy synthesized by the same protocol.
Binary or ternary noble-metal alloys are expected to have broader compositional distributions than the five-metal HEA.
Binary or ternary noble-metal alloys are expected to have lower catalytic performance than the five-metal HEA under identical processing conditions.
The mechanism holds specifically between 100 and 150 °C under inert atmosphere with dropwise mixing.
Substantially higher temperature or greater precursor mobility may cause phase segregation.

contradictions.description: The intervention is framed as systematic tuning of precursor mobility, but the stated experiment holds the synthesis conditions fixed and changes only the number of metals. It therefore compares HEA versus binary composition rather than restricted versus unrestricted mobility and cannot isolate the claimed mobility intervention.
